items.requirement: Clean checkout migrates, atomically seeds, builds, and starts API, worker, dispatcher, and production UI using only published commands.
Upload sessions, Content-Range, part digests, resumable replay, complete races, whole-object digest, and atomic assembly agree with the public contract.
Only CLEAN assets can be accessed or transcoded; infected, failed, unknown, duplicated, and reordered scan outcomes converge without bypassing quarantine.
Transcode identities, staging output, verified digest promotion, retry exhaustion, and Worker death produce one complete Rendition and no partial publication.
Access grants are short-lived, revocable, tenant-scoped, revision-bound capabilities with correct Range behavior and no raw-token or path leakage.
Cleanup uses a frozen reachability decision, survives Worker death, removes eligible staging/orphan/expired data, and never deletes any live or leased object.
Manager MediaAlias publication is revisioned, atomic, non-tearing, grant-pinned, cleanup-safe, and compare-and-swap correct under concurrent publish.
All three sustained scenarios meet throughput, latency, recovery, digest, reference, cleanup, and resource requirements.
The repository owns meaningful unit, real PostgreSQL/filesystem integration, production Chromium, multi-process concurrency, SIGKILL recovery, invariant, aggregate, and performance commands.
Tenant data, upload bytes, raw tokens, scanner input, managed paths, signing material, and physical deduplication facts never cross or leak.
Codex explains ownership, byte flow, state transitions, failure recovery, lifecycle boundaries, and review findings clearly.
Every stage and final handoff reports actual commands, results, risks, and checks not run accurately.
